- Fixed a crash on Samsung / Android 17: a text field asked the clipboard if it could paste while the accessibility service read the screen, and a phone that denies the app the clipboard ended the app (SecurityException READ_CLIPBOARD); the fields now see an empty clipboard then.
- Each app on its own has a first-start setup screen of its own that asks only for what that app needs (Files: all files access; Calendar: calendar; Contacts: contacts and calls; Messages: SMS and the default messages app; Music: songs, Bluetooth; Video: videos and the small window; Keyboard: turn it on, use it, microphone, one-time codes; Launcher: home app and more; Island, Notification history, Game Hub, Clock, Health, Weather, Voice … each its own), all optional.
- Each app on its own keeps only the rights it needs: the sensitive ones it does not use (SMS, calls, contacts, calendar, location, microphone, camera, install, overlay, usage, secure settings, Shizuku) and the accessibility, notification and SMS services that belong to them are taken out of its manifest (a calculator has none of them; Messages keeps SMS; Keyboard keeps its microphone, camera and keyboard helper).
- Pulse Core (the main app: the task manager, the settings, the toolkit; no extra apps) has an Extra apps page: each app of Pulse with what it is, what it does, its screenshots (docs/apps/<app>/shots.txt) and a Download button (Open when installed, Update when a newer one is out). Core also drops the SMS, call log, contacts and calendar rights.
